dedupe_keys.name: buskit bus analytics toolkit for bunching mitigation

description: buskit is a Python toolkit for bus data streaming, analytics and simulation aimed at mitigating bus bunching. It fetches real-time bus positions in the SIRI format, stores historical trajectories, and provides a simple simulation environment in which operation strategies such as holding or stop skipping can be tested on real-time, historical or artificial trajectories to see their effect on headways and passengers. The author is Yuwen Chang, a research engineer at the Living Analytics Research Centre of Singapore Management University. Coverage: designed and tested with New York City bus data; the README says it can be adapted to other cities that publish GTFS and SIRI. Access: source on GitHub and a pip package (version 1.0.0.dev7). Licence and cost: MIT, free. Caveats: the README states the project is undergoing major restructuring, the simulator is described as a prototype still under development, and the package is a development release, so it is best treated as a research code base. It supports operations and control studies of bus service reliability and disruption recovery, and uses the kind of feeds catalogued under the MTA open data and the GTFS specification records.
